title: Terror cells forming in Negev Bedouin communities in 'concering phenomenon,' Shin Bet chief warn
body: Head of the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) David Zini warned during a Political-Security Cabinet meeting on Monday of unprecedented terrorist organization efforts in Bedouin communities in the Negev.In his remarks to cabinet members, the head of the service detailed that the defense establishment often identifies attempts to create infrastructure of a military nature inside Israeli territory. "There are places in the Bedouin diaspora with military infrastructure that we are constantly thwarting, attempts to establish quasi-military battalions; this is a very concerning phenomenon," he said.The warning comes against the backdrop of increasing involvement of Israeli citizens from Bedouin communities in terrorist incidents, in arms smuggling along the Egyptian border, and in ties with terrorist elements in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.Shin Bet and Police officials have identified that the spillover of illegal weapons on a massive scale into the Negev, alongside processes of nationalist and religious radicalization, has created fertile ground for the rise of local armed organizations.Officials from the defense establishment pointed to several key trends fueling the phenomenon: Weapons smuggling has turned the Negev into a procurement hub for standard-issue weaponry, including assault rifles, standard explosive devices, and night-vision gear.In addition, the line between criminal and nationalist activity is blurring: infrastructures that began as criminal organizations and protection-racket operations are undergoing radicalization processes and turning their weapons toward attempted terror attacks.'Right under your noses, armed militias capable of slaughtering Israeli citizens'Hamas and ISIS propaganda on social media has led youth from the Bedouin communities to establish local cells and attempt to emulate operational patterns of terrorist organizations in the West Bank.Targeted counterterrorism efforts by the Shin Bet, Police, and the IDF in Bedouin communities continue, including nighttime arrests, weapons seizures, and the use of advanced intelligence tools to cut short attempts to establish these "battalions" while still in their initial organizational phases.On Monday, during a conference held in Rahat with the participation of retired Major General Yoav Segalovitz, former Deputy Minister of Public Security and second on the Ra'am list, bursts of gunfire were heard nearby as part of an intra-clan conflict in the city."During the meeting, bursts of gunfire were heard right next to us, in the early evening hours. The inconceivable thing is that here in the city, this has almost become routine. Just yesterday, bursts of gunfire were heard for eight consecutive hours," Segalovitz said, adding: "Such a thing must not become routine. This is a severe failure of the government, which has abandoned the personal safety of its citizens."The Amcha Yisrael party, led by Ofer Winter, responded to Zini's warning that "the report regarding the Shin Bet chief's warning about attempts to establish military battalions in the Bedouin diaspora is supposed to serve as a flashing red flag for the Government of Israel and the defense establishment." Winter further added, "Where is the Prime Minister? Where is the Minister of Police?"Winter continued his attack, stating, "Right under your noses, armed militias capable of slaughtering Israeli citizens are being formed. What are you doing about it? The stinging failure to confiscate weapons in the Arab sector will blow up in our faces. No misconceptions and no excuses. The time for decisive resolution has come. The time for Winter has come," he urged.Bedouin leaders respond to Zini's commentsThe head of the Hura Local Council, Habes Al-Atawna, responded to Zini's comments, telling Walla that "there is no such thing among us. Even the timing, twenty days before the elections, is very strange. This is a democratic election campaign, and the timing of making such statements is because of the elections. Most Bedouins are law-abiding people to the law, and contribute to the state. There is criminality among a small minority, but this is under no circumstances terrorism. That small percentage has been neglected for decades."Ahmad, a resident of Rahat, expressed outrage over the Shin Bet chief's statement."Unfortunately, the heads of the defense establishments are also not helping to calm tensions or halt the incitement against the Bedouins. We have always pleaded for the phenomenon of illegal weapons in Arab society in general, and among the Bedouins in particular, to be combated, with no response. The Bedouins in the Negev are waiting to receive recognition for their villages and treatment of their problems so they can live in dignity like human beings. If it turns out that there is any criminal or nationalist organizing, we all condemn and oppose it."The Regional Council of Unrecognized Villages also reacted to the Shin Bet chief's words, claiming they stem from political considerations."The entire country already knows that Zini has turned the Shin Bet into a branch of Likud, with all the accompanying lies. These headlines were not drafted in the Shin Bet offices, but in the office of Yonatan Urich, and they are completely fabricated from A to Z. A total spin whose sole purpose is to add a few votes of Arab-haters to the coalition of disasters. We view this unprecedented incitement with utmost severity."Ra'ed Al-Qian, a resident of Hura and a social activist, said they have been sounding alarms for years regarding illegal weapons, gunfire, and violence in Bedouin society. "We have repeatedly pointed out the scale of the phenomenon and the heavy price in human lives, but the governmental response was inadequate. Over the past decade, many Bedouin citizens have paid with their lives, so this cannot be viewed merely as an issue of policing and enforcement," he said."The fight against violence requires deep, cross-systemic intervention. Alongside resolute enforcement, what is needed is education, employment and vocational training, urban planning and housing, infrastructure and public services, leisure and sports frameworks, and opportunities for youth," Al-Qian said.He added that "when planning and housing solutions have been lacking for years, and instead families are primarily met with enforcement against unpermitted construction, one must also examine the link between planning policy and social reality."The question is not just how many weapons were seized and how many suspects were arrested, but what is being done today so that in five years there will be fewer weapons and less violence, and more education, employment, personal safety, and hope," he concluded.

title: Iran should reduce uranium enrichment capacity to end war with US — vice president
body:
WASHINGTON, October 7. /TASS/. Iranian authorities should significantly reduce their uranium enrichment capacity in order to end the war with the United States, US Vice President JD Vance said in an interview with Reuters .
"If you don’t want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don’t build highly enriched fuel. That’s a very basic threshold issue [when ending the conflict]," Vance said. "I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity."
He said the United States remained open to reaching an agreement but would demand concrete concessions from Iran in the nuclear sphere. "We’re not going to trade words for actions," the vice president said. In his view, the situation is complicated by the fact that Washington is unsure who makes decisions in Tehran. Vance said the United States was holding talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. However, he claimed, it was unclear how much influence they wield within Iran’s power structure. "One of the things we picked up on is it’s not totally clear how their country makes decisions," Vance said.
The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding envisaging an immediate ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, the United States resumed large-scale attacks on Iran overnight to July 8, having accused it of breaching the existing agreements in what concerned the Strait of Hormuz, a global chokepoint for approximately 25% of oil and some 20% of LNG supplies.
The Donald Trump administration recently signaled an end to any large-scale use of force against Iran and a transition to putting economic pressure on the Islamic Republic through sanctions instead.

title: Brazil to stay in BRICS after elections — Russian Federation Council speaker
body:
TURKMENBASY, Turkmenistan, October 7. /TASS/. Brazil will not leave BRICS after the elections as the association benefits all its members, and its leadership should understand this, Russian Federation Council Speaker Valentina Matviyenko said.
She called BRICS an "established, globally recognized association" that is gaining strength and momentum, "enjoys authority in the world and plays a very important role."
"And more and more countries are recognizing this and want to become members of BRICS. Whoever comes to power in Brazil cannot fail to understand that participation in BRICS is a great benefit for Brazil because they have gained tremendous opportunities for mutually beneficial international cooperation and for developing their economy, where no one imposes someone else's will, where there is no dictate. This association is built on mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation. And it seems to me that whoever comes to power - it would be a big mistake if they were to somehow reconsider their participation in BRICS. I am sure that this will not happen because any elected head of state should be guided above all by national interests and the well-being of their people, and BRICS is precisely a benefit for all its members, including Brazil," she said.
Russia, Matviyenko stressed, "never interferes in the internal affairs of any country," proceeding from the premise that the decision regarding the future head of state is up to the people of Brazil. "Of course, we would like to believe that this is exactly what will happen, that foreign manipulators will not interfere in the elections and attempt to change the will of the Brazilian people," she said.
The runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro is scheduled for October 25.

title: Dutch Defence Ministry Confirms Ukraine Aid Is Undermining Army Readiness and NATO Goals
body: Military assistance provided by the Netherlands to Ukraine is having a significant effect on the combat readiness of the Dutch armed forces and is complicating the country’s ability to fulfil NATO military capability targets, according to the Dutch Ministry of Defence. The ministry described the effect of military assistance to Ukraine as a “displacing effect” on the readiness of the Dutch armed forces and the fulfilment of NATO objectives. The ministry declined to publicly identify which NATO targets had been delayed or affected or provide details of the current readiness level of individual Dutch units. The admission provides an indication of the growing tension between providing military equipment to Ukraine, and maintaining national inventories at the levels required for a major conventional conflict. The Dutch experience reflects a broader problem across NATO. European armed forces entered the war in Ukraine with inventories designed primarily for peacetime requirements and relatively short high-intensity contingencies. Six years of sustained Ukrainian demand for artillery ammunition, air-defence interceptors, anti-tank weapons, armoured vehicles and other equipment have exposed limitations in both stockpiles and industrial production capacity. According to the Dutch Defence Ministry, the country had provided approximately €11.7 billion in military support to Ukraine by February 2026. Artillery ammunition has been one of the most visible examples, with European countries have supplied Ukraine with millions of rounds, which new production has been far from sufficient to replenish. The extreme depletion of European arsenals has gained growing attention as tensions with Russia have escalated. German officials speaking to the Wall Street Journal in March warned that the country has been left poorly protected against potential air or missile attacks due to the transfer of military systems, and particularly MIM-104 Patriot l ong range air defence systems, to Ukraine. The issue has been exacerbated by the more recent deployment of remaining Patriot systems to protect Poland on NATO's eastern flank from late 2025. Germany was alongside the Netherlands and the United States one of the first three countries to donate Patriot systems to Ukraine in early 2023. In April 2024 German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock confirmed the exhaustion of the country’s capacity to make further donations, stating: “Unfortunately, the stocks, especially our own Patriot systems, are now pretty much exhausted. Therefore I made it clear at a NATO foreign ministers’ meeting that we need to check the availability of all Patriot systems in Europe and globally, and that we will make every effort to obtain these systems for Ukraine.”

title: Iran must cut enrichment to end war, US uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran, Vance says
body: US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the country's seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.Vance, a longtime skeptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for US President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections.Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns."If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said."I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity."Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms.Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions."We're not going to trade words for actions," Vance said.Unclear how Iran makes decisions, says VanceComplicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran.Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. But it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran's power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei."One of the things we picked up on is it's not totally clear how their country makes decisions," Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday his "biggest problem" is no one knows who is running Iran.Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran's decision-making system works."The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference.Vance rallies for Alaskan candidate says he's unsure if he will run for presidentVance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through the waterway.The war — and its $3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress.Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump's handling of the conflict, telling voters they should not let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month's elections.In Alaska, Vance rallied for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024, but rising everyday costs have put the state in play.Before speaking with Reuters, Vance focused much of his speech on affordability concerns, especially around energy. Alaska's remote locale makes consumer goods more expensive, and energy production is a key industry.Rally attendees roared when Sullivan nearly introduced Vance as the president of the US, rather than the vice president. Vance is seen as a leading Republican contender to succeed Trump in the White House.Vance told Reuters afterward that he had not decided whether to seek the presidency in 2028."I'm inherently a procrastinator," he said. "I really haven't thought about it much."

title: EU now sliding toward becoming military bloc — Russian Federation Council speaker
body:
TURKMENBASY, Turkmenistan, October 7. /TASS/. The European Union is becoming a military bloc today despite having been created as a single economic community, and people in EU countries are dissatisfied with this, Russian Federation Council Speaker Valentina Matviyenko told reporters, commenting on growing protest activity in a number of EU countries.
She said people are taking to the streets "out of desperation," protesting against a European bureaucracy that has "practically deprived European states of their sovereignty." People are protesting because their politicians "are not fighting for the national interests of their countries" but addressing geopolitical problems "invented by someone."
"People are also dissatisfied with the ongoing militarization of Europe," she said, citing German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's public statement that he does not care what the German people think. She called these "very alarming trends," adding that abandoning cheap hydrocarbons brought about this situation, which is "a road to nowhere, a dead end."
Earlier, protests by high school students began in the Paris region of Ile-de-France and spread across France against overloaded schedules, teacher shortages, and other education problems. In some places, they escalated into riots and clashes with police, with nearly 2,000 people detained and 1,800 in custody.
Protests also took place in various Spanish cities amid the housing crisis. On September 26, a major demonstration was held in Madrid following the eviction of an elderly woman, forced to leave her rented home after 70 years. Hundreds set up a tent camp in the capital's central square. It was later reported the woman would be able to return home after reaching an agreement with the property owner. Similar protests were subsequently organized in other cities.

title: America’s Newest Fighter Makes First Flight: How Capable is the F-16 Block 72?
body: The first F-16 Block 72 fighter has completed its maiden flight, with the aircraft being closely related to the F-16 Block 70 that first flew in January 2023. The principal distinction between the two enhance dF-16s is their engines, with the Block 70 aircraft use General Electric’s F110-GE-129, while Block 72 aircraft are powered by Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 engines. The two versions otherwise share the same major avionics and systems modernisation package. Morocco became the launch customer for the configuration when the U.S. government approved its request for 25 F-16C/D Block 72 aircraft in March 2019, meaning the program has taken more than seven years to reach the first flight stage. The Royal Moroccan Air Force is currently the only client in the world for the Block 72 variant. Procured under a package with an estimated $3.787 billion value, the F-16 Block 72 fighters cost are being exported for approximately $151.5 million each including the costs of spare parts, maintenance infrastructure, and weaponry, making them among the most expensive lightweight fourth generation fighters ever sold. Morocco already operates F-16s, making the acquisition of additional aircraft in the latest configuration an extension of an established fleet rather than the introduction of an entirely new fighter type. The Royal Moroccan Air Force has previously operated F-16C/D Block 52 aircraft, while the country has also pursued upgrades and additional combat aircraft to modernise its air force. Although the F-16 has increasingly been criticised as obsolete by many of its operators from Singapore to the United States, with the U.S. Air Force having itself ceased acquisitions in 2005, the fighter represents a low cost option for clients with lower defence budgets unable to acquire its successor the F-35 or higher end F-15EX heavyweight fighter. Among economically developed clients the only one to have purchased the new F-16 variant is the Republic of China Ministry of Defence, largely due to political restrictions on its acquisitions of F-35s due to its status in both the UN and Washington as a non state actor. Morocco previously selected the F-16 Block 50/52 over rival Western fighter types, including the French Rafale, and is scheduled to upgrade these older F-16s to a similar avionics standard under the F-16V program. The F-16 Block 70’s ability to influence the balance of power with neighbouring Algeria will be limited, as the Algerian Air Force already fields a very large fleet of ‘4+ generation’ fighters, namely Su-30MKA and Su-35 which are considerably heavier and carry radars close to three times as large as those of the F-16 while have tremendous advantages in nearly all performance parameters. The Algerian Air Force brought its first Su-57 fifth generation fighters into service in late 2025, before the Moroccan Air Force had even operationalised ‘4+ generation’ fighters, with the gap in air power expected to continue to grow. Although NATO members across the Mediterranean continue to be considered the primary potential threat to Algerian security, particularly after their assault against neighbouring Libya in 2011 caused mass destruction and permanently destabilised the country, the Su-57 fleet also has significant utility against Moroccan forces. The Moroccan Defence Ministry has been reported by multiple sources to be interested in acquiring F-35 fifth generation fighter aircraft from the United States, as the country’s fleet sees its standing continue to diminish in the face of neighbouring Algeria’s rapidly expanding aerial warfare capabilities. A growing number of Moroccan sources have called for the country to seek to leverage its ties with Israel to gain access to the F-35, which has only been sold to four non Western countries including South Korea, Japan, Singapore and Israel itself. In November 2021 a meeting between Israeli Defence Minister Benny Ganz and his Moroccan counterpart Abdellatif Loudiyi saw the two further defence agreements, and reportedly followed expressions of interest by Moroccan King Mohammed VI in acquiring F-35s with Israel’s help. It has been speculated that procuring the F-16 Block 72 could be seen as a stepping stone to later acquiring the F-35A, which would provide a broadly peer level capability to Algeria’s currently operational Su-57s.

title: US arrests person in connection to Canada school shooting, officials say
body: US authorities arrested a person in Washington state on Tuesday whom they accuse of providing advice and offering to live-stream a deadly mass shooting carried out earlier this year in Canada.James Cody Bryant, 30, was detained on a charge of conspiracy to murder people in a foreign country in connection with the shooting at Tumbler Ridge, according to the US Justice Department. The charge carries a penalty of up to life in prison.Bryant was in repeated contact with the shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, offering technical advice, sending money, including for the shoes to be used during the attack, and agreeing to live stream the event, law enforcement officials said."James Cody Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to, and he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer," Acting US Attorney for the Western District of Washington Neil Floyd told reporters.Court records did not immediately list an attorney for Bryant.Nine people, primarily children, were killed in the school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in one of Canada's worst mass shootings.Van Rootselaar, 18, who had suffered a series of mental health problems, killed her mother and stepbrother at home before shooting dead a teacher and five young students at her former school in Tumbler Ridge, a settlement of around 2,400 in the Canadian Rockies, according to police. Van Rootselaar, who police said was born a male but began identifying as a woman, then died by suicide.Bryant, who officials said they understood was also born a man but identified as female, agreed to live stream a feed of the attack and broadcast it "in a way that would maximize notoriety for the shooter," Mike Herrington, FBI Seattle special agent in charge, said.The live stream on Twitch was shut down after about 20 seconds, officials said.Shooter was dependent on Bryant's help, Herrington alleges"Without Bryant's misplaced loyalty and willingness to operate the live stream, we don't ultimately know if the shooter would have gone through with the crime," Herrington said."We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the live stream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the live stream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media."

title: Kyiv Rocked by Repeated Russian Missile Attacks Overnight After Zelensky’s ‘Massive Strike’ Warning
body:
Multiple explosions rocked Kyiv in repeated waves in the early hours of Wednesday as Russia launched ballistic missiles toward the Ukrainian capital, with damage reported across several districts.
A Kyiv Post journalist in the capital reported several strong explosions after the Ukrainian Air Force warned that ballistic missiles were heading toward the city.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Several hours later, Kyiv was rocked by explosions for a second time. Ukrinform reported renewed blasts at around 5:12 a.m., shortly after the Air Force detected several more ballistic missiles heading toward the capital. The air raid alert remained in force.
The attacks came only hours after President Volodymyr Zelensky warned in his nightly address that Ukrainian intelligence had received updated information indicating Russia was preparing a “massive strike.” He urged residents to take missile alerts seriously and said Ukrainian forces were ready to respond “as much as our defenses allow.”
Ukraine’s Air Force warned of ballistic missiles heading toward Kyiv, Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia after reporting a threat from Russia’s Bryansk region and from the south.
The overnight assault also included jet-powered drones moving across several regions. The Air Force tracked such drones over northern Kyiv region, while cruise missiles were later reported over the Kharkiv and Poltava regions.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko and the Kyiv City Military Administration reported damage in several districts as the attack unfolded.
In the Obolonskyi district, a strike was recorded in an area of non-residential development.
In Podilskyi, warehouse facilities were hit and damaged.
In Darnytskyi, burning debris fell on an open area, while in the Shevchenkivskyi district another strike hit a non-residential area.
The Kyiv City Military Administration later reported further consequences of the attack in Darnytskyi, where damage was recorded on the territory of a garage cooperative.
Air defenses were operating over the capital as officials repeatedly urged residents to remain in shelters.
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
The second round of explosions came several hours after the initial ballistic missile attack.
Shortly before the renewed blasts, the Ukrainian Air Force detected several ballistic missiles heading toward Kyiv.
The repeated explosions formed part of a broader overnight Russian assault in which missiles and fast-moving drones were tracked across multiple regions of Ukraine.
The latest attack comes as Kyiv faces an intensifying Russian air campaign approaching winter.
Russia has increasingly targeted Ukraine’s energy and transport infrastructure, including railways, roads and bridges over the Dnipro.
The capital has also endured repeated daytime and nighttime drone attacks in recent days, while air raid sirens have sounded for prolonged periods and forced residents into shelters, basements and metro stations.
Scheduled power cuts had already plunged parts of Kyiv into darkness Tuesday evening in an effort to reduce strain on the damaged electricity grid.
Russian forces have also repeatedly struck Kyiv’s bridges in recent days, disrupting road and metro traffic across key crossings over the Dnipro.
Zelensky said Tuesday evening that Ukrainian intelligence had fresh information about Russian preparations for a large-scale attack.
“There is updated intelligence regarding Russia’s preparations for a massive strike,” he said, urging Ukrainians to respond to missile alerts.
He also stressed that Ukraine’s ability to repel incoming missiles remained dependent on continued weapons deliveries from allies.
The warning was followed later Tuesday by reports that three Russian Tu-160 strategic bombers had taken off from the Belaya air base.
Hours later, ballistic missiles were heading toward Kyiv and other major Ukrainian cities, followed by renewed explosions in the capital before dawn.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Air Force: Russia may eventually accelerate jet-powered drones to 900 km/h
body:
Pilots need special skills to intercept such targets, so jet drone manufacturers have already been asked to develop simulators for crew training.
According to Ukrinform, Colonel Yurii Cherevashchenko, deputy commander of the Ukrainian Air Force’s air defense sector, reported this during a meeting of the Temporary Investigative Commission.
“We predict that the speed of Russian jet drones could reach 800–900 km per hour. Such speeds have not yet been detected,” he noted.
According to Cherevashchenko, pilots must possess certain skills to maneuver when intercepting such targets. At the same time, if the target’s speed and the interceptor’s speed are roughly the same, the pilot does not perceive the difference in speed as significantly.
The deputy commander added that, to train crews, a corresponding task has already been assigned to jet drone manufacturers. This involves creating simulators that will allow pilots to practice their skills in dealing with such targets.
As reported by Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine is destroying about 57% of jet-powered drones and between 85% and 90% of conventional drones, and is also testing five models of interceptor drones.

title: UN should clarify criteria for neutral state status — Russian Federation Council speaker
body:
TURKMENBASY, Turkmenistan, October 7. /TASS/. The United Nations should clarify the criteria for the status of a neutral state and update the concept in line with modern realities so that it is not "blurred," Russian Federation Council Speaker Valentina Matviyenko told reporters.
According to Matviyenko, Switzerland, which has traditionally been considered a neutral state, is moving away from this status because it follows the European Union’s directives and supports what she described as illegal sanctions, resulting in the "erosion" of the concept. Switzerland is not the only country behaving this way in today’s turbulent world, Matviyenko noted.
"I think the time has come for the United Nations to once again analyze its documents and provisions and ensure that if a state has permanent neutrality status, it strictly complies with all international rules established by the UN Charter and adheres to them. Perhaps the status of a neutral state should be clarified, perhaps updated in light of what is happening, so that the concept is not blurred and does not become merely decorative," she said.
At the same time, Turkmenistan, as the Federation Council speaker noted, is a genuinely sovereign state pursuing an independent and balanced foreign policy in the interests of its country and people. It is a state that does not succumb to any pressure, is not beholden to anyone and does not support illegal sanctions, she said. "This is exactly how countries with neutral state status should behave. And I want to say that Russia highly values Turkmenistan’s consistent position in maintaining permanent neutrality," she said.

title: Satellite images show renewed activity at secret Iran nuclear site bombed by IDF
body: Satellite imagery taken on Thursday showed significant renewed activity at a site in Iran called Minzadehei, believed to be linked to the development of nuclear weapons, just northeast of Tehran, after Israel struck the site in March, according to The Institute for Science and International Security.The institute reviewed high-resolution satellite images of the nuclear weapons facility from VANTOR Technologies. The imagery uncovered regular vehicle activity around the site, and extensive cleanup efforts after Israeli strikes in March destroyed several buildings and likely underground structures as well.The site, identified by the IDF as Minzadehei, is located on the northeastern outskirts of Tehran. IDF Chief Spokesman Brig.-Gen. Effie Defrin said in March that the site was linked to Iran's nuclear weapons development efforts. The IDF said intelligence had tracked Iranian nuclear scientists traveling to the site before the strike.More activity at sites allegedly connected to Iran's nuclear programThe IDF said the compound was designed to restore technology and advance capabilities needed to develop nuclear weapons, although it did not identify the specific component being developed there.The facility contained aboveground buildings and structures built into the surrounding hillside. The Institute for Science and International Security said satellite imagery showed a highly secured compound with buildings, roads, and structures partially embedded in the hillside.The renewed activity at Minzadehei comes as other signs have emerged of Iran rebuilding parts of its nuclear program.In September, Israeli intelligence presented information indicating that Iran was carrying out new construction at the Pickaxe Mountain site, a mountainous facility south of Tehran that has been identified as a possible location for restoring parts of Iran's nuclear program. The reporting did not establish that uranium enrichment was taking place there.Yonah Jeremy Bob and Idan Kweller contributed to this report.

title: Flydubai hijacker studied in UK, New Zealand, Australia, countries investigating - report
body: Hamam al-Hammami, the copilot accused of trying to hijack and crash a flydubai aircraft bound for Israel, studied to become a pilot in Britain, The Telegraph reported on Tuesday. Hammami trained with L3 Airline Academy, now a part of Acron Aviation, a pilot-training company with centers in Britain, including in Southampton and Bournemouth, as well as a simulator center near Gatwick, according to the report.L3 also had a relationship with Oman Air, where Hammami worked until February 2025, with the airline having named the aviation school as one of five internationally recognized institutions whose graduates would qualify for Oman Air's pilot recruitment program, the Telegraph wrote. Hammami was fired from Oman Air for views described as too close to Islamic extremism before being hired by flydubai eight months ago. Acron Aviation neither confirmed nor denied having enrolled Hammami, telling the Telegraph it did not disclose whether individuals were current or former students. “We were saddened to hear of this incident, and our thoughts are with everyone affected. As a matter of policy, we do not publicly comment on whether any individual is or has been a student with us," a spokesperson told the Telegraph, adding that the company would assist relevant authorities in any way they could. Hammami studied in Australia, UK, and New ZealandHammami referred to his education in the UK in a now-deleted Twitter account where he said he had "studied in Australia, Britain, and New Zealand for five years." He also spoke about his experiences with "European feminists."His Twitter account included posts advocating for violence against women and severe restrictions regarding marriage, dress, and working outside the home. New Zealand Police are now investigating Hammami's time spent in the country, according to the New Zealand Herald, which cited Police Assistant Commissioner Michael Johnson on Monday morning.“Police are aware the co-pilot spent time in New Zealand, and we are looking into the time he spent here, alongside other agencies where appropriate,” Johnson told local media. “We are unable to comment further at this time."Investigation underway into Hammami's radicalizationAustralian authorities are currently conducting an investigation into whether or not Hammami had been radicalized while in the country."The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team (VIC JCTT), comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO, can confirm it is investigating the man's links to Australia. An update will be provided at an appropriate time," an Australian Federal Police (AFP) spokesperson said, referring to the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation.The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Hammami had allegedly visited radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation.Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to the FT.Miriam Sela-Eitam contributed to this report.

title: October 7: Hamas’s profit-and-loss statement - opinion
body: On August 3, Ghazi Hamad, a member of Hamas's political bureau, sat across from Piers Morgan for a half-hour interview. Most viewers remember the denial. Hamad said he was “100%” confident that Hamas never committed crimes against civilians, and that whatever happened at the Nova music festival, in the kibbutzim, and in the homes set on fire was, at most, a “mistake” by individuals.The denial was shocking, and rightly so. It was also the predictable part of the interview. The important part came some 15 minutes later, when Morgan asked whether October 7 had been a strategic failure, given what it brought down on Gaza.Hamad conceded that “we paid a big price” and moved straight to the profit column. Israel is isolated. Its prime minister is wanted by the International Criminal Court. And, in his words, “All the world now, they put the Palestinian cause on the table.” Before October 7, he said, there were only Security Council meetings and Arab statements that changed nothing on the ground. Now there are “strategic achievements.” He closed the answer by saying Hamas had not changed.This was a profit-and-loss statement, delivered by one of the people who signed off on the investment.The massacre dividendFor Hamas, the massacre was an investment. The killing, the rape, and the abductions were meant to provoke a harsh Israeli response, the images from Gaza that followed, and the international pressure those images would generate. Call it the massacre dividend: the political return a terrorist organization extracts from its own atrocity once the world translates it into urgency to “solve the issue.”Gazans paid the price. Hamad himself left the Gaza Strip before October 7 and never went back, as he acknowledged in the same interview. The dividend is being collected in European capitals, and Washington may be next.Whoever rewards a massacre with statehood is inviting the next one, and not only in Israel. Paris and London are within range as well.The Israeli wallOn the Israeli side, the picture is the reverse. The Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs has measured public opinion seven consecutive times over 30 months. Opposition to a Palestinian state has held steady at 64% to 68% of the public, and at 75% among Jewish respondents in the latest wave. Total support, including conditional support tied to recognition and demilitarization, has not exceeded 25% in any survey.One figure is rising sharply. Concern about an October 7-style attack from Judea and Samaria climbed from 62% in February 2025 to 77% in September 2026. Even among left-wing respondents, a majority now shares that concern.A poll captures attitudes at a given moment and cannot predict how the public will respond to sustained pressure. But three years on, this is no longer post-traumatic shock. Israelis understood Hamad's sentence better than most of the West: a state established now would be credited to the massacre.Pressure from outsideEurope reads the same map and draws the opposite conclusion. In September 2025, the European Commission proposed suspending part of Israel's trade preferences under the EU-Israel Association Agreement. The proposal stalled, and Spain's attempt to revive it in spring 2026 ran into broad opposition. Yet the economic lever is now legitimate in Brussels, and it has advanced alongside a wave of European recognitions of a Palestinian state. All this on a continent where the Islamist voice, in the street and at the ballot box, grows louder every year.In Washington, the process is slower, but it cuts across party lines. If Democrats retake Congress in November's midterms, the wing that wants to condition aid to Israel and impose sanctions will gain committees, budgets, and a platform. And on the same Morgan episode, Joe Kent, former director of the National Counterterrorism Center, called for ending American funding of Israel and spoke of a new political movement on the Right. By 2028, the issue will be on every candidate's desk.Hamad was right about one thing: the issue is back on the table. The question is who will pay for it, the slaughtered or the slaughterers.What is requiredFor anyone who still believes a Palestinian state would end the conflict, Hamad supplied the answer in the same interview. When Morgan told him he supports a two-state solution and a full Palestinian state, Hamad shot back: “So why should Israel exist?”At the end of the interview, when asked three times for a yes or no on whether he still believes Israel should be annihilated, he would not say no. Instead, he called Israel “a big burden on the shoulder of the world” and said the world “should reconsider the existence of Israel.”For Hamas, a Palestinian state is a stage. The destination has not moved.Jerusalem must stop treating recognitions of a Palestinian state as symbolic gestures, and should put Hamad's words before every international forum: Hamas itself is declaring that recognition is a reward for October 7. European capitals must understand that every economic measure against Israel tied to the demand for statehood is recorded in Gaza as a return on the investment. In Washington, in both camps, anyone who talks about sanctions should answer one question: How much is he willing to pay an organization that has openly admitted the massacre was worth it?The writer is the communication director of the Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs (JCFA) and a former senior editor in Israeli and international media.

title: Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike is conscious and speaking, lawyers say
body: Convicted killer Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by lethal injection last week, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries, has regained consciousness and is speaking, her lawyers said in a statement on Tuesday.Despite severe injuries to her arms from the insertion of intravenous lines during the attempted execution last Wednesday, Pike, 50, is "still handcuffed and shackled" to her hospital bed while she remains under medical care, her team of public defense attorneys wrote."Her prognosis remains unclear, but at a minimum we expect a long recovery," the lawyers' statement said, adding that a court hearing on Pike's case was scheduled for Wednesday in Davidson County Chancery Court.Pike, sentenced to death for her role as a teenager in the torture-murder of a 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer three decades ago, survived the botched execution attempt on the night of September 30 at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital. She has been hospitalized since then.Her lawyers said on Friday that their client remained unconscious, critically ill, and hooked to a ventilator to breathe, as doctors labored to clear the drug pentobarbital from her system.Pike first person in the US known to survive execution drugs"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking and continues to receive critical medical care," they wrote on Tuesday.Pike's petition for clemency, denied last week by Governor Bill Lee, argued that her death sentence had failed to properly account for Pike's own childhood trauma as the victim of sexual abuse, neglect, and untreated mental illness.Pike went from being the first woman Tennessee had tried to put to death since the early 19th century to becoming the first person in the United States known to have survived after execution drugs were administered.Death penalty opponents said the incident exposed the inherent barbarity of executions. It also highlighted the difficulties of carrying out lethal injections while respecting constitutional prohibitions on cruel and unusual punishment.'None of it was normal' Pike's attorneys and journalists who witnessed the execution attempt described it as roughly 2-1/2 hours of disarray and prolonged distress for her as Department of Correction personnel struggled to administer two doses of pentobarbital intravenously."None of it was normal," Catherine Sweeney, a reporter for Nashville public broadcaster WPLN, recounted. "It went really poorly."Pike was heard gasping, crying, whimpering and breathing loudly through much of the procedure, at one point saying, "my arm feels like it's about to burst open."The bungled attempt to establish intravenous lines left both of Pike's arms "swollen, burned and blistered," the apparent result of the pentobarbital, a highly alkaline and caustic substance, seeping into the tissues under her skin, her lawyers said in court filings.The lawyers accused state officials of having shrugged off prior warnings from Pike's doctors that her small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis would make placing IV lines especially difficult.In the midst of the procedure, Pike's lawyers filed an emergency court motion seeking to halt the procedure. By then, prison officials had ceased their execution efforts and called an ambulance, according to court records.The night of the execution attempt, the Department of Correction defended its handling of the situation, saying it had "followed every step of the state's lawful, established execution protocol." But the governor said agency commissioner Frank Strada has resigned and will leave his post this month.Lee had previously ordered a suspension of any scheduled executions for the rest of the year and a third-party review of what happened in Pike's case.Two days before Pike was due to meet her fate, Lee rejected a petition seeking to commute her death penalty to a life prison term without the possibility of parole.Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, her 17-year-old boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, and a third companion lured Slemmer into a wooded area on the University of Tennessee campus in Knoxville and killed her.The gruesome nature of the slaying, which involved Shipp carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim's chest and Pike bashing Slemmer in the head with a chunk of asphalt, then taking a piece of her skull as a souvenir, drew intense media coverage at the time. Trial testimony indicated that Pike viewed Slemmer as a rival for her boyfriend's affections.Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder. Pike was sentenced to death, while Shipp received a life sentence with the possibility of parole.Their co-defendant, Shadolla Peterson, who was 18 at the time of the murder and had acted as a lookout for the other two, testified for the prosecution and received probation.

title: Russia’s Shadow Fleet Tanker Burns off Sochi After Black Sea Attack
body:
A Liberian-flagged oil tanker caught fire off Russia’s Black Sea resort city of Sochi on Tuesday evening after what Russian authorities described as an attack by an unmanned vessel, sending flames and thick black smoke over the coastline.
Russia’s Transport Ministry said the Aframax Rio was struck at sea and that crude oil was burning in the Black Sea. All 23 crew members – Indian nationals – were rescued without injuries. Firefighters initially struggled to approach the vessel because of the intensity of the blaze.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Videos and photos circulating on Russian social media showed bright orange flames offshore and a towering column of black smoke visible from Sochi.
The blaze was intense enough to prevent firefighters from immediately tackling it, AFP reported.
Authorities restricted access to beaches and sections of the coastline as smoke from the burning tanker spread toward Sochi.
The fire was visible from across the resort city, while emergency services monitored the vessel and surrounding waters.
The incident brought the escalating Black Sea maritime conflict directly to Russia’s southern coast, where shipping and energy infrastructure have increasingly come under threat.
The Aframax Rio has been identified by Ukraine as part of Russia’s so-called shadow fleet – a network of tankers used to keep Russian oil exports moving despite Western sanctions, price caps and other restrictions imposed after Moscow’s full-scale invasion.
Kyiv sanctioned the vessel in February, saying ships in the network help Russia preserve vital energy revenues that fund its war against Ukraine.

title: Air Force: Intensive use is rapidly shortening F-16 service life
body:
According to Ukrinform, Colonel Yurii Cherevashchenko, deputy commander of the Ukrainian Air Force’s air defense division, made this statement during a meeting of the Verkhovna Rada’s Temporary Investigative Commission.
When asked whether Ukrainian aircraft, particularly the F-16s, are actively engaging Russian jet drones, Cherevashchenko said: “The F-16 is one of the most effective means of countering jet UAVs.”
At the same time, he was asked whether maintenance and the service life of the aircraft are the main challenges for the F-16s . He confirmed this and explained that aircraft have a limited service life, and Ukrainian planes are being used at an extremely high rate.
“Therefore, keeping the aircraft in a constant state of readiness is a very difficult task. And here, the assistance of our partners is critically important,” the deputy commander emphasized.
When asked whether Russian jet drones are being destroyed directly at their bases and launch sites, Cherevashchenko noted: “In general, the best option here is to destroy them at their bases and launch sites, the so-called drone ports. We’ve already carried out several such strikes. But these are heavily fortified facilities, reinforced with concrete, so it’s not easy to take them out. This is one of the key components of countering jet-powered UAVs.”
As reported by Ukrinform, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten stated after a phone call with President Volodymyr Zelensky that the Netherlands would assist Ukraine with maintenance, spare parts, and ammunition for F-16 fighter jets.

title: Trump claims to be in procces of mulling whether to end conflict with Iran 'the nice way'
body:
WASHINGTON, October 7. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump said he was considering whether to end the conflict with Iran "the nice way."
"We have to finish up [the conflict with Iran], and it’s only a question of which way: do we want to do it the nice way or the not so nice way? And pretty soon you’ll find out," the US leader said while speaking in Baltimore, Maryland.
"The biggest problem I have is nobody knows who the hell is running the country. Nobody knows, but maybe that’s a good thing. But you remember [former Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic Ayatollah Ali] Khamenei. They’re all gone," the president added. According to him, Iran’s "missile drone manufacturing capacity is way down." "It’ll soon be gone. We know exactly where the rest of it is," Trump said.
He added that he gets "calls all the time from the leaders of the world" thanking him. According to Trump, he responds "‘Good. When are you going to pay for it?"
The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding envisaging an immediate ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, the United States resumed large-scale attacks on Iran overnight to July 8, having accused it of breaching the existing agreements in what concerned the Strait of Hormuz, a global chokepoint for approximately 25% of oil and some 20% of LNG supplies.
The Trump administration recently signaled an end to any large-scale use of force against Iran and a transition to putting economic pressure on the Islamic Republic through sanctions instead.

title: At least 2 killed Kyiv as Russia slams capital with missile, drones on Putin's 74th birthday
body:
Editor's note: This is a developing story and is being updated.
At least two people have been killed in Russia's overnight mass missile and drone attack on Kyiv on Oct. 7, coinciding with Russian President Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday.
The Kyiv City Military Administration reported that the casualties occurred in the Darnytskyi district of the capital.
Multiple explosions were first heard in Kyiv around 3:15 a.m. local time, according to Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground. Ukraine's Air Force previously warned of several Russian Tu-95 bombers approaching the border.
"The missiles are falling one after another. At least 10-12 explosions from what I can count. It's pretty loud in the city center," the Kyiv Independent's Tim Zadorozhnyy described.
Other Kyiv Independent journalists described strikes around Kyiv's Podil district with flames and smoke seen in the capital.
Explosions were again heard two hours later at 5:15 a.m. amid a second wave of missile attacks.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that a strike was reported at an unspecified "non-residential area" in the Obolon District, while warehouse facilities were hit in the Polid district.
Missile debris was also burning in the Shevchenkivskyi district, while in the Darnytskyi district, a garage caught fire.
The full extent of the damage caused was not immediately clear.
Earlier, drones headed towards Ukraine's capital at 9 p.m. local time, Ukraine's Air Force reported , and an air raid alert was announced in the city shortly after, lasting from 9:09 p.m. until 9:58 p.m.
Elsewhere in the country, a Russian missile reportedly damaged a residential building in the community of Kremenchuk in Poltava Oblast. While in the eastern city of Zaporizhzhia, transport infrastructure was reportedly damaged amid the large-scale attack, officials reported.
The full extent of the damage caused was not immediately clear.
President Volodymyr Zelensky earlier in the day urged citizens to take air raid alerts seriously and warned that Russia is preparing a large-scale attack on Ukraine, citing recent intelligence.
"Please, please, take care of yourself. Please respond to signals of missile danger," he said.
The latest large-scale attack come as Putin turns 74-years-old on Oct. 7. The average male life expectancy in Russia is 68 years as of 2024, according to the World Bank Group.
Russia attacked Kyiv the previous night, damaging cars , and has targeted the city's key bridges in recent days.

title: US Senator Murphy says Pentagon denied him access to US base in Qatar
body: Democratic US Senator Chris Murphy said on Tuesday that the US Defense Department denied him access to a key military base in Qatar during a visit to the Middle East, describing it as part of a US government effort to conceal the impact of the Iran war.The Al Udeid Air Base is the largest US base in the region and has repeatedly been attacked by Iran during the war launched by the US and Israel in February."This trip confirmed for me that there is an active, unprecedented, unconstitutional effort underway to hide the costs of this war and the implications of this war from Congress and the American people," Murphy told a group of journalists in Riyadh, the second stop on his trip.Many members of Congress, including some of President Donald Trump's Republicans, have been pushing his administration to provide them with more information about the cost of the war, strategy and casualties.Asked for comment, a senior Pentagon official said Murphy's office had been informed before his trip that he would not receive the department's support to access the base, consistent with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth's March 3, 2026, directive restricting travel to the area."The Department applies the Secretary's guidance evenly," the official said in an emailed statement.Murphy said that the Pentagon refused to set up a briefing for him on the war while he was in the region.'Never encountered anything like this,' Murphy claims"I've never encountered anything like this in my time in the Senate, and it's part of a deliberate campaign of obfuscation that my Republican colleagues in Congress should demand an end to," he said.He said that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had facilitated his visit, including arranging meetings with diplomats, a stance he contrasted with that of the Pentagon.During his trip, Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee who represents the state of Connecticut, met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al Thani and with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as well as other senior Gulf officials.

title: Russia to take retaliatory measures if Canada confiscates Russian assets — ambassador
body:
MOSCOW, October 7. /TASS/. Russia will respond immediately if Canada confiscates Russian assets, Russian Ambassador to Canada Oleg Stepanov said.
In an interview with Izvestia , the diplomat recalled that Bill S-214 on sovereign assets completed its Senate stage on May 26 and moved to the House of Commons for consideration. At the same time, Bill C-219 is being developed, providing for the disposal of assets belonging to sanctioned individuals and entities, including the possibility of transferring them to state ownership.
"It is difficult to say what the authors mean by ‘Russian assets,’ and where in Canada they intend to look for them. In any case, Russia’s position on such encroachments on property, whether in Canada or elsewhere, is well known. Such actions are illegal and will prompt an immediate response from our side," Stepanov stressed. In the ambassador’s view, "politicians in Ottawa should, more broadly, consider the legal, investment and reputational consequences for their country of such ‘lawmaking.’"
The diplomat also addressed the property dispute over the An-124 RA-82078 aircraft operated by Volga-Dnepr Airlines, which has been at Toronto airport since February 2022. "The company continues to seek the return of the aircraft through legal means. Our position remains unchanged: the aircraft must be returned to its owner, and if it is confiscated, Russia reserves the right to take retaliatory property-related and other measures," the ambassador explained.

title: Deep Purple brings five decades of rock to Athens on 13 October
body: Deep Purple will play Telekom Center Athens on 13 October 2026, their only Greek date, with the rising British act Jayler as special guest The band has spent more than 50 years as one of hard rock’s defining names: a long run of records, sold-out rooms, and a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. “Smoke on the Water” and “Highway Star” are still the songs the set is built around. “Child in Time,” first released in 1970, has had a second life in the trailer for the new season of Stranger Things , which put the track in front of a younger audience. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Deep Purple (@deeppurple_official) The Athens show also follows the 2024 album =1 , the latest sign that the group is still recording as well as touring. title: Church Denies Russian Troops Lost Dmitry Donskoy Relic
body: A fragment of the right hand of Dmitry Donskoy, sent to the front by the Russian Orthodox Church last month, is now the subject of a missing-relic claim that the church calls a fabrication. The military has not commented. No recent photograph from the front has been published, so neither version can be checked. Reliquary said to hold a fragment of the relics of Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy British intelligence revised its estimate of Russian casualties since February 2022 — killed, wounded and missing — to 1.5 million. General Sir Richard Knighton, chief of the defence staff, said most of those losses had come since January 2023, a period in which Russia has taken about 2 per cent of Ukrainian territory. The Center for Strategic and International Studies put Russian battlefield casualties at up to 450,000 this summer. A February 2026 estimate put Ukrainian military casualties, dead and wounded, at 250,000 to 300,000. In nearly two decades in Vietnam, the United States lost 58,220 dead, with 303,704 wounded and 1,584 missing. The church’s attempt at a morale lift came on 8 September. The Moscow Patriarchate’s department for the armed forces said a reliquary with part of the relics of Grand Prince Demetrius Donskoy was on its way to the front, “to stand invisibly, in battle formation, alongside our defenders.” The fragment was found last summer during restoration at the Archangel Cathedral in the Kremlin. Donskoy is honoured in Russia for the victory over the Mongols at Kulikovo in 1380. The church declared him a saint in 1988. On 1 October, the Moscow Times, now based in Amsterdam after being expelled from Moscow, reported that two pro-war Telegram channels had written that retreating troops abandoned the remains. Church spokesman Vakhtang Kipsindze told the state agency RIA Novosti that the reports were a fabrication, spread to harm the church. Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi has retaken about 68 square miles around Lyman, in northern Donetsk, and captured 250 Russian soldiers. In a sector under constant drone attack, a report that troops came under fire during a prayer and left the reliquary is at least plausible. The war the relic was sent to bless has included more than 3,000 attacks on hospitals and other health facilities, more than 3,900 children killed or injured, and, according to the United Nations, the systematic abduction and transfer of thousands of children from Ukraine to Russia and Belarus. If a saint’s hand was meant to inspire an invading army, its loss is an awkward reading. Source: skai.gr The post Church Denies Russian Troops Lost Dmitry Donskoy Relic appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Access to coastline restricted in Odesa region
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Odesa Regional Military Administration announced this on Facebook .
The administration said that in the Odesa region, the start and end of the recreational season are determined by joint orders of the "Odesa" Operational-Tactical Grouping and the Odesa Regional Military Administration.
"These orders determine the sections of the Black Sea coast that have undergone safety inspections and are permitted for visitors. After the season ends, the relevant order expires, and access to the designated beach areas is restricted," the administration said.
The administration explained that the measures are related to safety. After the season ends, the relevant services no longer continuously monitor water safety, inspect the seabed, check the territory for explosive objects, or operate lifeguard stations.
"In this regard, we ask residents and visitors to refrain from visiting beach areas," the administration said.
As Ukrinform reported, 48 beach areas were officially opened in Odesa region during the summer of 2026. Of these, 47 were located in Odesa and one in Chornomorsk.

title: Christa Pike faces lengthy recovery after botched execution attempt — lawyers
body:
NEW YORK, October 7. /TASS/. Christa Pike, who survived a botched execution attempt in the US state of Tennessee, faces a lengthy recovery, her lawyers said after their client regained consciousness.
"Her prognosis remains unclear, <…> she faces a long recovery," Pike’s lawyers said in a statement cited by Associated Press .
They described what happened to Pike as "medically unprecedented" and noted that "despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed."
On September 30, Pike was scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in over 200 years on Wednesday. However, she was rushed to a hospital following two failed attempts to administer the drugs.
Christa Pike was 18 years old at the time of the crime in 1995. She and her accomplice were convicted of the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, who attended the same educational institution as Pike. According to the prosecution, Pike feared Slemmer was pursuing her boyfriend, lured her to a secluded area, where she and her accomplice tortured and killed her. The case drew widespread attention due to the brutality of the murder, the age of the participants, and the fact that a satanic symbol was carved into the victim’s body.
